Practice 02

Ownership, governance and succession should be designed as one structure, not three.

HAYKALAH structures how families and sovereign entities hold, govern and pass on their assets: holding companies, boards, waqfs and the vehicles beneath them. We also find the land and buildings that cost money to hold, and put them to work. The practice serves family offices, trusts and family-owned groups, as well as ministries, authorities and government-owned companies.

What we do

  • Holding structures that separate ownership, management and the operating companies.

  • Governance for families and their companies: boards, decision rights and reporting.

  • Succession and continuity planning across jurisdictions, including holdings outside the Kingdom.

  • Family and charitable waqf design: establishment, nazir governance and income distribution.

  • Portfolio reviews that identify idle land and under-used buildings for the asset-monetization engine.

  • Board representation on funds and companies.

  • For sovereign partners: development-company establishment, asset-program design and PPP consortium architecture.

  • Screening of new opportunities with HOAM before capital is committed.

How we create value

  • 02

    Monetization

    We review portfolios to find the idle land and under-used buildings that cost money to hold, and put them to work through the asset-monetization engine.

  • 03

    Optimization

    We screen new opportunities with HOAM before capital is committed, and use a holding company, waqf or SPV where each fits.

  • 05

    Transformation

    We design ownership, governance and succession as one structure, form the companies and seat the boards, then keep the structure working through board representation and regular reporting.

How we work

  1. 01

    Map

    We list the assets, the entities, the objectives of the family or institution, and the rules that apply in each jurisdiction.

  2. 02

    Design

    One structure covers ownership, governance and succession, with a holding company, waqf or SPV where each fits.

  3. 03

    Coordinate

    Legal, Shariah, tax-and-Zakat and accounting advisers work to one plan, which HAYKALAH manages.

  4. 04

    Implement

    Companies are formed, boards are seated and documents are signed.

  5. 05

    Monitor

    Board representation and regular reporting keep the structure working as the family or the program changes.

Questions

What is the difference between a family waqf and a charitable waqf?

A family waqf directs its income to the founder’s family and descendants. A charitable waqf directs it to charitable or public purposes. A joint waqf does both, in the shares the waqf deed sets.

What does a nazir do?

The nazir administers a waqf. The nazir manages its assets, collects the income and distributes it to the beneficiaries as the waqf deed requires.

Can HAYKALAH sit on a fund or company board?

Yes, as a governance role. Managing the fund itself stays with the fund’s CMA-authorised manager.

How does HAYKALAH work with government entities?

HAYKALAH designs asset programs, development companies and PPP consortium structures for ministries, authorities and government-owned companies. Programs described on this site are at framework or proposal stage unless stated otherwise.

Can the first conversation be confidential?

Yes. You can ask for an NDA before you share any details, and HAYKALAH does not name clients on this site without their written consent.

Start with a confidential conversation. An NDA can come first.
